title: I Used the Sheep-Shearing Stand Log on the Lead Who Hijacked My Numbered Combs

parts.text: I stepped into the shearing floor at 7:08 a.m. and lead Hugh was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE STAND. FORTY MINUTES. COMBS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was thirty-four, farm secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered combs. Hugh shrugged. "Leads are the combs." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover cutters on my numbered combs. Then I asked for the stand log. At 7:16 the floor pinged why Hugh's name was on my cutters. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The floor can see Hugh's leftover cutters on my numbered combs.

social.video_title: He hijacked my numbered shearing combs on my stand — Part 1/2
social.description: Shearing floor, leftover cutters, a forty-minute clock he posted. I logged the combs. Would you have asked for the stand log?

parts.text: Hugh called it second cuts until the floor asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the cutter still. The combs went back to my numbered slot. Hugh ran a slot of his own and told the next lead atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: LEADS ARE NOT THE COMBS. I keep my combs in a labeled tin. Hugh brown-bags his second cuts. The floor finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Leads are not the combs — Part 2/2
social.description: Stand log, numbered combs, and a second line on the board. Was a second cut ever my cutters?
